checklist_item: Re-run scripts/mission_ren_iphi_attrition.py and reproduce 6/57 = 10.5%
claim_as_stated: 6 of 57 iPhi sponsors exited 2023-Nov 2026 (10.5%)
validator_primary_source_url: scripts/mission_ren_iphi_attrition.py (live --fetch rerun, outputs redirected to scratch); https://dns.google/resolve
exact_values_found: No cache was shipped, so I ran a live --fetch rerun with output redirected to scratch: population_n 57; status_counts active 49 / migrated 6 / unknown 2 / lapsed 0. Exits: Arkansas CF, Acadiana, Gulf Coast CF (Venice), Greater Flint (all to Foundant CommunitySuite), WaterStone (to Give Interactive), Yakima Valley (to akoyaGO). attrition_point 0.10526 (6/57); Wilson 95% 0.0491-0.2112; dated-only 5/57 = 8.8%; with the 2 unknowns (BNY Mellon CGF, Ayco) 8/57 = 14.0%; annualised 2.83%. ren-iphi-tenant-census.csv has the same 76 rows and keys as the repo copy, with zero status differences. Summary population, status, exits and point estimate are identical
discrepancies: None in the numbers. Four of the six exits (Acadiana, Flint, Arkansas, Yakima) are classified from the repo's own cf-vendor-migrations-2022-2026.csv (manual input), so the rerun alone cannot verify them independently. My live checks (V11-01b-g) do confirm all four destinations. The doc's 'Flint (about 2026-01 [I])' sits beside a census row dated 2026-01-20, and both are inferred
interpretation_challenge: No cache was shipped, so 'cached mode' could not be used and the rerun needed live DNS and HTTP. Live state can drift between runs. Gulf Coast CF (Venice) is counted as an exit, but its iPhi page only says the new portal is 'launching soon'. The 57 is a census of tenants that could be found (DNS guesses, CT logs, path probes and 990 payees), not Ren's client list. Treat 10.5% as a lower-information estimate. The Wilson 95% interval of 4.9-21.1% is correct.

checklist_item: Re-run scripts/mission_net_payout.py; recompute pooled figures
claim_as_stated: Pooled FY2021-24 ex-processors: gross 23.9%; net 21.5% (A), 20.8% (B), 19.0% (C); nationals 23.8% -> 20.9%; 12.1% of national DAF grants go to other nationals
exact_values_found: The rerun parsed 7,559 returns (6,161 ok, 19 no 990). Its net-payout-by-sponsor.csv is byte-identical to the repo copy. I recomputed independently from the rows. Ex-processor itemized (3,373 sponsor-years, 1,002 sponsors, $825.8bn BOY): gross 23.93%, A 21.50%, B 20.80%, C 18.96%. Nationals itemized (204 sponsor-years): gross 23.78%, A 20.91%, B 20.08%, C 17.98%, tier-A transfer share 12.08%. On the all-in-sample basis, ex-processor gross is 23.71%
discrepancies: The doc gives n = 3,421 sponsor-years, 1,018 sponsors and $831bn BOY next to the ex-processor percentages. Those counts are for the 'all' sample, which includes processors (its gross is 25.4%). The ex-processor sample is 3,373 / 1,002 / $825.8bn
interpretation_challenge: 'Go to other nationals' means tier-A recipients (DAFRC National/Standard). Grants to Fidelity and the like are counted as transfers whether or not they fund DAF accounts. Tier C at 18.96% rounds to 19.0%
